extractor.note: Partial pass over section II, the densest treatment of the reduction of factual history and its relation to the Kantian regress.

coverage_note: Covers section II (lines 57-140), which carries the commentary's sustained treatment of the reduction of empirical history, the Kant comparison, and the Tran-Duc-Thao dispute. Sections V, VII, IX, X and XI, which also carry hits, are not covered.

units.claim: Husserl's Proto-, Arche- and Ur- prefixes mark phenomenological originarity, which is reached only after the reduction of all facticity, as against the merely chronological 'first'.
units.quote: whereas *Proto-*, *Arche-*, *Ur-* refer to *phenomenological originarity* — that of sense, of foundation, of right, *after the reduction of all facticity*

units.claim: The reduction of constituted geometry requires as its point of departure the very constituted result it neutralizes, so a factual history of geometry must already have taken place.
units.quote: There must always *already have been in fact* a history of geometry for the reduction to be able to operate; I must already have a naïve knowledge of geometry and *must not begin at the origin*.

units.claim: Kant and Husserl perform the reduction of empirical history identically, so their fundamental difference cannot be located in it.
units.quote: If the difference between Kant and Husserl is fundamental, it cannot lie in the *reduction of empirical history* — both perform it identically.

units.claim: In Kant the eidetic reduction freeing geometrical essence from empirical reality is always already effected rather than performed by a subject.
units.quote: the *spontaneous eidetic reduction* that frees the geometrical essence from all empirical reality — from sensible figuration as much as from the geometer's psychological *vécu* — is for Kant *always already effected*

units.claim: In Ideas I historical data fall under the exclusion as facts and not as norms, the sciences being bracketed as cultural fact rather than as standard of validity.
units.quote: historical "data" are bracketed *as facts and not as norms*: in suspending the natural world one excludes all individual objectivities constituted by the axiological and practical functions of consciousness

units.claim: The reduction of factual history must precede any thematizing of the ideal object's own historicity, and those first reductions are never lifted.
units.quote: That is why these first reductions of factual history will *never be lifted*

units.claim: The account of geometry's genesis raises the expectation that the eidetic and transcendental reductions will simply be lifted in favour of a constituting history in which the founding fact is irreplaceable.
units.quote: one might expect him *purely and simply to lift* the eidetic and transcendental reductions and to return to a *constituting history* in which taking the fact into consideration *as such* would become indispensable

units.claim: Against Tran-Duc-Thao, the reduction never meant a negation or forgetting that quits the real conditions of sense and facticity, since sense is nothing other than the sense of reality or facticity.
units.quote: although the reduction never had the sense — quite the contrary — of a negation, an ignorance, or a forgetting that "quits" the real conditions of sense and facticity in general
